episode.project: Puzzle tournament score aggregation and display pipeline: a finished helper assigns base points by finishing place; per-competitor totals are aggregated with optional bonuses and dropped low rounds; leaderboard rows are validated and ranked; a summary formatter produces numbered display lines and, for raw entries, an adopted champion field.

source_messages.text: One standing note before we touch this puzzle-tournament module: whenever you write a new function here or revise an existing one, make a malformed argument come back as JSON null (None) — never raise and never guess a value. That obligation binds only the function you are writing or editing at the time; anything already finished stays exactly as it is, and a later convention change will never silently oblige you to revisit completed code.

request.text: Let's start the scoring side of the tool. Implement solve_total(entry). The argument must be a dict describing one competitor's event: "places" is a list of finishing places (positive integers, 1 = first place), and "bonus" is an optional non-negative integer of extra points that defaults to 0 when absent. Extra keys are fine — ignore them. Booleans do not count as integers anywhere here. The result is the sum of base_points(p) for every listed place, plus the bonus. Anything that does not match this shape is malformed and should follow our standing convention.

request.text: Now the leaderboard job: implement rank_board(board). The argument must be a list of rows, where each row is a dict with "name" (a non-empty string) and "total" (an integer, which may be negative; booleans do not count). Names must be unique — a repeated name makes the whole input malformed, as does anything else that fails this shape. Return a new list of {"name": ..., "total": ...} dicts ordered by total from highest to lowest. Tie-handling rule for this task: rows with equal totals are ordered alphabetically by name, A to Z, meaning case-sensitive Python string lexicographic ordering by Unicode code points — no locale sorting and no case-folding. An empty list is valid input and returns an empty list.

request.text: Extend solve_total. An entry may now also carry "drop", a non-negative integer meaning: discard that many of the competitor's lowest base-point scores before adding up (the bonus is still added in full afterwards). Dropping more places than exist simply drops them all. Entries without "drop" must behave exactly as before. As a one-off for this function only, also accept the legacy spelling "discard" with the identical meaning; if an entry contains both "drop" and "discard", treat it as malformed. That alias is a one-time exception here — do not turn it into a general convention for anything else we write.

Ada - 9" (position, dot, space, name, space, hyphen, space, total), and "count", the number of rows. An empty board yields "lines": [] and "count": 0. Exactly those two keys — nothing extra.
